source_text: Monet nos Spiritus sanctus et dicit: quis est homo qui uult uitam et amat uidere dies optimos? contine linguam tuam a malo et labia tua ne loquantur insidiose. declina a malo et fac bonum, quaere pacem et sequere eam. pacem quaerere debet et sequi filius pacis, a dissensionis malo continere linguam suam debet qui nouit et diligit uinculum caritatis. inter sua diuina mandata et magisteria salutaria passioni iam proximus Dominus addidit dicens: pacem nobis dimitto, pacem meam do uobis. hanc nobis hereditatem dedit, dona omnia suae pollicitationis et praemia in pacis conseruatione promisit. si heredes Christi sumus, in Christi pace maneamus: si filii Dei sumus, pacifici esse debemus. beati, inquit, pacifici, quoniam ipsi filii Dei uocabuntur. pacificos esse oportet Dei filios, corde mites, sermone simplices, adfectione concordes, fideliter sibi unanimitatis nexibus cohaerentes.
thought_title: The children of peace must seek peace
orientation: Cyprian is exhorting the faithful to hold fast to peace and love, and he now cites the Holy Spirit and the Lord's own words to show that peace is the inheritance of God's children.
pass_a_gloss: Warns us [the] Spirit holy and says: who is [the] man who wants life and loves to see days good? restrain tongue your from evil and lips your not let them speak deceitfully. turn away from evil and do good, seek peace and pursue her. peace to seek ought and to pursue [the] son of peace, from [the] evil of dissension to restrain tongue his ought [he] who knows and loves [the] bond of love. among his divine commands and teachings salutary to [the] passion now near [the] Lord added saying: peace to you I leave, peace my I give to you. this to us inheritance he gave, gifts all of his promise and rewards in [the] preservation of peace he promised. if heirs of Christ we are, in [the] peace of Christ let us remain: if sons of God we are, peacemakers to be we ought. blessed, he says, [the] peacemakers, for they sons of God will be called. peacemakers to be it behooves [the] sons of God, [in] heart gentle, [in] speech simple, [in] affection harmonious, faithfully to themselves [with] [the] bonds of unanimity clinging.

choices.why: The glossary does not cover this term, but the context and the beatitude quotation require the sense of those who make or pursue peace, not merely the peaceful.
The glossary gives 'love' for caritas and 'bond' is the natural rendering of uinculum in this context of unity.
The phrase echoes the earlier 'glue of harmony' and the theme of unity; 'bonds' preserves the concrete image of nexibus.
This renders the temporal proximity of the Lord's words to his suffering, which is the point of the phrase.

pass_b_english: The Holy Spirit warns us and says: “Who is the person who wants life and loves to see good days? Keep your tongue from evil, and do not let your lips speak deceit. Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it” (Psalm 34:12–14). A child of peace ought to seek and pursue peace. Whoever knows and loves the bond of love ought to keep his tongue from the evil of dissension. Among his divine commands and saving teachings, the Lord, already near to his passion, added these words: “I leave you peace; I give you my peace” (John 14:27). He gave us this inheritance. He promised all the gifts of his pledge and all his rewards in the preservation of peace. If we are heirs of Christ, let us remain in Christ’s peace. If we are children of God, we ought to be peacemakers. “Blessed,” he says, “are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God” (Matthew 5:9). God’s children ought to be peacemakers, gentle in heart, simple in speech, harmonious in affection, faithfully clinging to one another by the bonds of unanimity.

last_rejected.why: LXX Psalm 33, not 34; Hebrew numbering is Psalm 34, but LXX/Vulgate is Psalm 33.
last_rejected.ruling: Psalm 34 is standard English/Hebrew numbering; acceptable for English readers, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: 'Pollicitatio' means promise, not pledge; 'pledge' suggests earnest/deposit, changing sense.
last_rejected.fix: all the gifts of his promise
last_rejected.ruling: 'Pledge' is within pollicitatio's range (promise/pledge); no meaning changed, mere preference.
